Package org.aeonbits.owner.formats.toml

package org.aeonbits.owner.formats.toml
Reads a configuration written in TOML v1.0.0 - a source whose path ends in .toml - flattening it into the keys the rest of the library already speaks.

Of the formats here this is the one that needed the least persuading: the flattening convention was already shaped like TOML. A dotted key is the flattening, [table] is a prefix, and [[servers]] is servers[0], which is what a List of nested configuration objects reads.

Values are handed back as written, except where TOML spells one value several ways. 1_000, 0xDEAD, 0o755 and 0b1101 are all one integer and none of them would convert, so they become plain decimal; inf and nan become what Double.parseDouble(String) answers to; and the space TOML allows in place of the T of a date-time becomes a T, which is what LocalDateTime.parse(CharSequence) wants. Strings are untouched.
